overall: Violation found: the Hamilton Finance and Advisory Committee held a Oct. 19, 2013 meeting on a notice posted less than 48 hours ahead, with no valid emergency. Intentional, so referred to hearing with a recommended $500 fine, plus a compliance order.

allegations.summary: Committee met Oct. 19, 2013 to review Special Town Meeting warrant articles, but the notice was posted only about 38 hours ahead, short of the 48-hour rule.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by holding a meeting without posting a notice at least 48 hours before the meeting.

allegations.summary: Committee argued an emergency justified the short notice because it had to meet a deadline before the Board of Selectmen's October 21 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Although the Committee was working to meet a deadline, the circumstances were not of the sort that justify an emergency meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint implied the violation was knowing: the Chair was warned by email and in person before the meeting and proceeded anyway, so the violation was intentional.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee acted with specific intent to violate the law because the Chair was informed via email and in person, prior to the October 19, 2013 meeting, that the meeting lacked proper notice, yet chose to proceed with the meeting in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law ordered.
Matter referred to a hearing under 940 CMR 29.07(3), with a recommended $500 civil fine for the intentional violation under G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c).
remedy_passage: Additionally, we order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
